title: What sugars are in honey?

seo.title: What sugars are in honey? Fructose, glucose and more
seo.meta_description: Honey does not contain just one sugar. Fructose and glucose dominate, with smaller amounts of sucrose, maltose and other sugars.
seo.search_intent: Learn which sugars make up honey, their approximate proportions, and what that composition means nutritionally.

excerpt: Honey is made mostly of fructose and glucose. In a broad USDA analysis of honeys, averages were about 38.4% fructose and 30.3% glucose, with roughly 17.2% water plus smaller amounts of maltose, sucrose and other sugars. Total sugars in typical honey are around 82 g per 100 g, so it is not pure sugar but it is a very concentrated source of simple sugars.
content_html:
Honey tastes uniformly sweet, but the sweetness does not come from one molecule. Inside the jar is a mixture dominated by fructose and glucose, along with water and much smaller amounts of several other sugars.

The exact proportions change with floral source, geography, and batch. Analyses of many honeys still give us a useful picture of what a typical jar contains.

Fructose and glucose make up most of honey's sugars

A USDA Agricultural Research Service composition study found averages of about 38.4 g of fructose and 30.3 g of glucose per 100 g of honey. Together they account for roughly 69 g—most of the sugar in the sample set.

Approximate componentPer 100 g honey
Fructose≈38.4 g
Glucose≈30.3 g
Water≈17.2 g
Total sugars≈82 g

The roughly 13 g of sugars beyond fructose and glucose are not one single compound. They include maltose, sucrose, and a variety of oligosaccharides whose proportions vary from honey to honey.

Why isn't honey mostly sucrose?

Flower nectar can contain sucrose, but bees add enzymes as they process nectar and much of that sucrose is split into glucose and fructose. Mature honey therefore usually contains much less sucrose than granulated table sugar.

Granulated sugar, by comparison, is almost entirely sucrose. Each sucrose molecule is one glucose unit linked to one fructose unit; digestion separates them before absorption.

The fructose-to-glucose balance helps determine texture

Glucose is less soluble in water than fructose. Honey with relatively more glucose tends to form crystals more readily, while a higher fructose-to-glucose ratio generally helps honey remain liquid longer.

That is one reason two honeys stored in the same pantry can behave differently. One may become creamy or grainy within weeks while another stays fluid for months, without that difference proving that either jar is fake or spoiled.

How much sugar is in a normal serving?

The 82 g per 100 g figure shows concentration, but you do not need to eat 100 g to get a substantial amount of sugar. A tablespoon weighing about 21 g contains roughly 17 g of sugars; a 7-g teaspoon contains about 5.7 g.

In U.S. nutrition labeling, honey used as a sweetener contributes to added sugars. Its glucose and fructose came from nectar, but that does not make honey equivalent to whole fruit, where sugars remain inside a food matrix containing water, fiber, and intact cellular structure.

The minor sugars add complexity, not a free pass

Honey can contain maltose, sucrose, turanose, trehalose, and other oligosaccharides. Researchers can even use detailed sugar profiles as clues to botanical origin and authenticity.

For everyday nutrition, however, the larger picture is straightforward: typical honey is about four-fifths sugar by weight. Its carbohydrate mixture is chemically more complex than granulated sugar and helps create its flavor, moisture behavior, and crystallization pattern, but honey remains a concentrated sweetener.

faq.question: What is the main sugar in honey?
faq.answer: Fructose is usually the largest individual sugar, averaging around 38% in the USDA analysis, followed by glucose around 30%. Exact proportions vary with floral source.

faq.question: Does honey contain sucrose?
faq.answer: Yes, but usually in much smaller amounts than fructose and glucose. Honey also contains maltose and several other minor sugars.

faq.question: How much sugar is in a tablespoon of honey?
faq.answer: A tablespoon weighing about 21 g contains roughly 17 g of sugars.
